concept_card.statement: A convex lens forms a full real image where rays meet, screen or not.
concept_card.analogy: Like a crowd using half the gates: everyone still gets out, slower.
steps: Each object point lights the whole lens, so covering part only dims the image.
Rays meet at v anyway; a screen just scatters them.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: If I cover the top half of the lens, the top half of the image disappears.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: Covering half a window hides half the view, so covering a lens seems to hide half the picture.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: Each object point sends rays to the whole lens, so the open half still brings light from every point to the image.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: Covering part of a lens still gives the full image, only dimmer.
remediation_cards.sim_moment: Lens Bench: switch on 'cover top half of lens' and watch the whole image stay, just fainter.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: If there's no screen, there's no real image. It just doesn't form.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: In the lab we only ever notice the real image when it lands on the screen.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: Rays meet at the image point with or without a screen; an eye or camera beyond it sees the image in air.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: A real image forms where rays converge; a screen only scatters its light so it can be seen from many angles.
remediation_cards.sim_moment: Lens Bench: remove the screen and watch the rays still crossing at the image point.

contrast_probes.probe: Half the lens is covered and the screen is taken away. What is left at the spot where the image was?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: Half an image is still there at that spot.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Nothing at all, because the screen is gone.

contrast_probes.probe: The image is sharp on the screen. You stick paper over the top half of the lens. What changes on the screen?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: Part of the image disappears and only half is left.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: The whole image stays but gets dimmer.

contrast_probes.probe: You remove the screen and put your eye some distance beyond where the image was, looking at the lens. Do you see the image?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: No, without the screen there is nothing to see.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Yes, I see the inverted image hanging in the air.

verify_flags: Covering half the lens roughly halves the brightness; sharpness may change slightly (aberrations/diffraction), which the cards ignore
Seeing an aerial real image needs the eye inside the cone of rays and at least about 25 cm beyond the image
